summary: Cold read of the recorded drill-panel contract and task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only) returned NOT CONVERGED with seven repository-resolvable findings and one open staging decision. All seven were folded into the contract and task plan; the staging decision - what leaf Actuals do inside the panel while the leaf drill is still task 3 - was put to the human, who chose plain non-focusable text with the prototype's guidance copy held back to task 3.

criteria_map.Every NON-LEAF Actual cell in the statem: Affordance boundary. The cold read found an inert underlined leaf link would be a false affordance while wiring it would cross into task 3; the human chose plain non-focusable text AND holding the 'Click any Actual to see its transactions' copy until task 3, so nothing on screen promises a behaviour this task does not deliver.
criteria_map.Clicking a non-leaf Actual opens the pan: The flatten, the block, and the no-network claim. The cold read found the descendant test could pass while always reading the default selected block, and that 'no network' was an inspection claim rather than a falsifiable proof; the criterion now requires a divergent FY-YTD fixture with assertions against the CLICKED block and an API-client spy asserting zero calls. The sort chip also now reads 'Statement outline order' instead of the prototype's 'Actual descending', which would misdescribe rows rendered in outline order.
criteria_map.The Grand Total opens the same way, by a: Grand Total special case, unchanged by the grill: grandTotal is a sibling carrying children: [], so the panel flattens response.tree roots.
criteria_map.The panel's Total row foots in EXACT PAI: Footing. The cold read found the story plan requires the drill footer to show rounded rupees with exact paise beneath, which the task had omitted, and that the derived zero-budget percentage labels needed direct tests rather than trust; both are now in the criterion, along with the explicit ban on Number() for money.
criteria_map.The panel matches the approved prototype: Dialog behaviour. The cold read found the prototype's scrim carries its own close handler and that 'focus trapped' was unproven; the criterion now names all five behaviours - initial focus, Escape, scrim click, a trap at BOTH Tab boundaries, and focus return.
criteria_map.The behaviour is proven by vitest leaves: Proof set. Required leaves went from four to seven to cover the block sensitivity, the zero-network spy, the nil-rule percentages and the full dialog contract.

current_flow: Today the statement renders as a role='treegrid' table: StatementRow recurses over node.children with aria-level, MeasureCells renders Budget, Roll-over, Actual and % as plain non-interactive td cells, and the grand total is a tfoot row using the same MeasureCells. Nothing in the table is clickable, formatMoney rounds every FixedScaleMoney to the rupee for display, and formatPercentage passes non-numeric labels through verbatim. Task 1 shipped the drill endpoint and its wire types, but no frontend code calls them. This task adds the first interactive cell in the statement and the panel it opens, reading only the MisStatementRunResponse already on screen.
new_abstractions: A drill panel component: the first modal dialog in this frontend, carrying focus management (initial focus, trap, return) that no existing surface needed.
A descendant-leaf flatten over MisStatementNode, with the Grand Total as a named special case because grandTotal sits beside the tree rather than in it.
Client-side paise arithmetic over FixedScaleMoney strings - integer paise via BigInt - as the footing check the panel's Total row rests on.
gaps: The story plan requires the drill footer to render rounded rupees with the exact paise beneath, but the task specified only formatMoney for the Total row, so it could ship without the paise line or a test for it.
The approved prototype's scrim carries its own close handler, but the task required only Escape and the close control, leaving scrim-click unspecified and untested.
'Focus trapped' was asserted but unproven: the required leaf covered only Escape and focus return, not initial dialog focus or the Tab and Shift+Tab boundaries.
The descendant-flatten test could pass while always reading the default selected measure block, since a single-block fixture cannot distinguish measures[0] from the clicked block.
'No network' was not a falsifiable proof - nothing spied the API client, so a stray fetch would pass review by inspection alone.

The Total row's derived percentage had no direct zero-budget cases, although the statement's nil rules (NA, over-budget, credit / negative actual) are established semantics and a label passed through a numeric formatter has shipped as NaN before.

The sort chip was to be copied from the prototype, whose level-one chip reads 'Actual descending', while these rows render in the statement's outline order - the drawn label would misdescribe the data.
contradictions: The task required the prototype's 'Click any Actual to see its transactions' guidance while making leaf Actuals inert until task 3: the copy would describe a behaviour the task does not deliver, and an underlined pointer-styled inert link would be a false affordance.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c4 now requires the Total row to render the rupee figure through the statement's formatMoney with the exact paise value on a secondary line, matching what the story plan settled for the drill footer.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c5 now names scrim-click alongside Escape, and the dialog required test covers it.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c5 names all five dialog behaviours (initial focus, Escape, scrim click, a trap at BOTH Tab boundaries, focus return) and the required leaf exercises each.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c4 and a new required leaf add a divergent FY-YTD fixture whose two blocks hold different numbers, with assertions against the CLICKED block; reviewer_focus calls out that a panel reading measures[0] passes every single-block fixture.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c2 makes the no-network claim falsifiable: a required leaf spies the API client across opening both a nested aggregate and the Grand Total and asserts zero calls, and reviewer_focus warns to check the spy targets the client the component actually uses.

REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c4 requires the three zero-budget cases to be tested directly and bans Number() for money, citing the NaN that mis-selection shipped by pushing a label through Intl.NumberFormat.
REPO-ANSWERED - criterion t-dp-c2 specifies a static non-interactive chip reading 'Statement outline order', recorded in the task plan as a deliberate, reasoned departure from the drawn label.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) - leaf Actuals render as plain non-focusable text with no underline, pointer or handler, in the panel as well as the statement, AND the 'Click any Actual to see its transactions' copy is held back to task 3, which is when clicking a leaf actually opens transactions. Rejected: keeping the prototype copy from task 2 (one task's worth of copy describing something that does not work) and wiring the leaves now (merges tasks 2 and 3, undoing the split the human approved).
open_items: Non-blocking - the panel ships with two recorded departures from the approved prototype: the sort chip label and the withheld guidance copy. Both are stated in the task plan so the functional check does not read them as design drift.

rounds.question: Task 2 renders the panel's leaf rows, but the leaf → transactions drill is task 3. The prototype draws each leaf's Actual as an underlined link and carries the copy "Click any Actual to see its transactions. Budget is not drillable." Shipping task 2 with that link inert is a false affordance; wiring it crosses the task boundary. What ships in task 2?
options: Plain text, and hold the copy too (Recommended)
Plain text, keep the prototype copy
rounds.chosen: Plain text, and hold the copy too (Recommended)

rounds.question: Closing the drill-panel task grill. Seven findings settled from the repo: the Total row gains the exact-paise line beneath the rounded rupees (as the story plan requires of the drill footer); the scrim closes the panel, as the prototype's own handler does; the focus trap gets real Tab / Shift+Tab boundary and initial-focus assertions; the descendant test gets a divergent FY-YTD fixture so it cannot pass while silently reading the default block; "no network" becomes falsifiable by spying on the API client and asserting zero calls; the Total row's zero-budget percentage gets direct NA / over-budget / credit-negative tests; and the sort chip reads "Statement outline order" rather than the prototype's "Actual descending", which would misdescribe the rows. Any remaining gap before I delegate?
